content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A security researcher operating under the pseudonym Nightmare Eclipse has publicly disclosed an unpatched Windows Defender vulnerability called ShieldBreak, days after accusing Microsoft of threatening legal action against researchers who disclose zero-days outside the company's own reporting process, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/12/after-microsoft-threatened-legal-action-a-security-researcher-publishes-a-new-windows-zero-day-bug/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece balancing the technical disclosure with the Microsoft dispute context. Correctly hedges on unresolved questions (legal action, patch timeline, researcher identity) in a 'What We Don't Know' section.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read TechCrunch and NVD snapshots directly; verified BleepingComputer (403, no archive.org fallback) via WebFetch. TechCrunch confirms the app-based exploit delivery, the Will Dormann verification detail, the May 2026 legal-threat blog post and its partial social-media walkback, and the Microsoft spokesperson quote verbatim. NVD confirms the RoguePlanet CVE description, both CVSS scores (7.0 NVD / 7.8 Microsoft), the affected version range, and both dates (published Jun 16, modified Aug 12) verbatim. BleepingComputer's claims (tested-vs-untested Windows versions, the cfapi mechanism, the Nightmare Eclipse quote, the nine-disclosures count, and the spokesperson quote) all verified via WebFetch.
